polities.name: Vandals (Hasdingi and Silingi) before Africa
polities.summary: Two Vandal groups, Hasding and Siling, from the middle Danube and Silesia, who crossed the Rhine with the Alans and Suebi in 406, settled in Spain in 411 and crossed to Africa in 429, becoming the Vandal Kingdom.

polities.name: Following of Radagaisus
polities.summary: Gothic-led coalition from the middle Danube that invaded Italy under the pagan king Radagaisus in 405 and was destroyed at Faesulae in 406.

polities.name: Isaurians
polities.summary: Mountain people of the Taurus within the empire, notorious raiders, who supplied soldiers and, under Zeno, an imperial dynasty; their power was broken in the Isaurian War of 492-497.

polities.name: Armenian princes (nakharars)
polities.summary: The Armenian noble houses (Mamikonian and others) after the end of the Arsacid monarchy in 428, ruling under Persian or Roman suzerainty and rebelling in 451 and 572; Armenian contingents fought for Rome at the Yarmuk.

polities.name: Western Turkic Khaganate
polities.summary: Western wing of the Göktürk empire founded in 552, allied with Constantinople against Persia under Istämi (embassy of Zemarchus, 569) and Tong Yabghu, whose forces joined Heraclius at Tiflis in 627.

polities.name: Muslim community of Medina
polities.summary: The polity led by Muhammad at Medina from the Hijra (622) to his death (632), which unified much of Arabia and fought the first clash with Rome at Mu'ta (629); succeeded by the Rashidun Caliphate.
